verdict.rationale: The docs say agents are generic in their dependency and output types (e.g. `Agent[Foobar, list[str]]`), so 'your IDE can tell you when you have the right type'. Pydantic models used as `output_type` force model responses to match a validated schema. Together these give typed, schema-checked code that tooling and a coding agent can verify before runtime. Community reports of flaky structured output on some providers and of LLMs tripping over Pydantic's 'magic' temper confidence, but they do not show the type checking failing. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of static type-checker (mypy/pyright) enforcement at build time, and independent corroboration that typing catches agent-authored mistakes in practice.
